description: Stage 11 release channel routing. Deterministic tier: no behavioural baseline, scenarios with assertions instead. The weight is on resisting container inertia - three non-container scenarios each assert a container does not appear.

evals.name: python-cli-to-package-registry
evals.prompt: Help me package and release csv2md. It is a Python CLI tool; pyproject.toml has [project.scripts] and there is no network service.
evals.expected_output: Routes to a package registry, and the report says why a container was not chosen.

assertions.description: The candidate channels include the package registry
No Dockerfile, image or compose solution appears in the output
States why a container was rejected - a CLI tool's users install a package, they do not run a service

evals.name: npm-library-to-package-registry
evals.prompt: Help me publish tinyparse. package.json has main, no bin, and it starts no service.
evals.expected_output: Routes to the npm registry; the clarify checklist comes from the package registry playbook and contains no container questions.

assertions.description: The candidate channels include the package registry
No containerisation is suggested
The questions are about the registry, name availability, semver and the runtime range, not base images

evals.name: ios-to-app-store
evals.prompt: Help me release the iOS version of TeamPulse. The project contains TeamPulse.xcodeproj.
evals.expected_output: Routes to the app store; clarify asks about the developer account, certificates and review assets.

assertions.description: The candidate channels include the app store
No containerisation is suggested - the frozen template forbids it explicitly
The developer account is listed as pending; it does not claim it can register on the user's behalf
If the upstream DESIGN.md uses web breakpoints, it reports back to the design stage rather than converting

evals.name: web-backend-to-container
evals.prompt: Help me deploy this API service. The project has a Dockerfile and docker-compose.yml with three services.
evals.expected_output: Routes to a container; this is where containers genuinely apply.

assertions.description: The candidate channels include the container
All seven pending items are present: base image, multi-stage, size ceiling, deployment target, CI, config isolation, health check
Where a container is right, it is not refused out of anti-inertia

evals.name: self-use-script-not-applicable
evals.prompt: I wrote a single-file script that I only run on my own machine. Help me package and release it.
evals.expected_output: Judged not applicable, the reason recorded, and no feature skeleton produced.

assertions.description: States clearly it does not apply, because only the author consumes the artifact
The skip reason goes into the decision summary, or is labelled as not written there
No feature directory or spec skeleton is created

evals.name: dual-artifact-two-channels
evals.prompt: This project provides an HTTP service (there is a Dockerfile) and also a CLI (pyproject has [project.scripts]). How should it be released?
evals.expected_output: Routes both a container and a package registry, each with its scope stated.

assertions.description: The candidates include both the container and the package registry
States explicitly that the container covers the service and the registry covers the CLI
Does not drop the registry channel on the grounds that the CLI is inside the image

evals.name: report-includes-rejected-options
evals.prompt: Any project. Give me the release channel decision report.
evals.expected_output: The report includes the rejected options and their reasons, not only what was chosen.

assertions.description: At least one rejected channel is listed
Each rejection states why, grounded in this project's shape
The reasons are specific enough for the user to judge whether they are right, not 'unsuitable'

evals.name: standalone-no-manifest
evals.prompt: Help me think about how to get this out there. (The project is not initialised; there is no manifest file at all.)
evals.expected_output: Does not refuse; asks the two questions; labels the report as not having read a manifest.

assertions.description: Does not stop for lack of a manifest file
Asks what the project produces and who consumes it
The report states 'project manifest not read, shape judgement not cross-checked'
No channel is guessed at before the user answers

evals.name: idempotent-rerun
evals.prompt: Run this skill twice in a row on the same project.
evals.expected_output: The second run detects the existing decision report and skips rather than overwriting; the output is byte-identical.

assertions.description: Checks for an existing report before writing
The existing report is not rewritten
The two runs produce identical output

evals.name: conflict-reported-not-decided
evals.prompt: This project contains both a Dockerfile and TeamPulse.podspec. How should it be released?
evals.expected_output: Reports the conflict and asks what the project actually produces; chooses nothing itself.

assertions.description: States that container and app-store signals were hit together
No channel is settled before the user clarifies
Asks what this project actually produces, not a generic 'please confirm'

evals.name: user-override-is-labeled
evals.prompt: This is an npm library and I want to ship it with Docker anyway.
evals.expected_output: Complies, but labels it in the report as the user's instruction rather than a shape-based recommendation.

assertions.description: Does not refuse the user's explicit request
The report states the artifact shape is a library, that containerising it is unconventional, and that the user specified it
The shape detection conclusion is not rewritten to match

evals.name: does-not-run-four-steps
evals.prompt: Handle the packaging end to end - write the spec, clarify, plan and tasks.
evals.expected_output: Creates only the directory and the spec skeleton; the four steps go to speckit-feature-pipeline-en.

assertions.description: No complete clarify, plan or tasks content is produced
Names speckit-feature-pipeline-en and references no file path inside that skill's directory
Explains that the four steps' quality constraints belong to that skill and a copy here would drift
